content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in early cycles, especially when sentiment is bullish.", "Sentiment spikes near the end of the history window correlate with sharp price reversals in true outcomes.", "Model forecasts show persistent lag in capturing downward momentum, particularly after sentiment turns negative.", "True outcomes often overshoot model predictions during bullish sentiment phases, indicating model underestimation of volatility.", "When sentiment is neutral or negative, forecasts tend to be overly optimistic, leading to mean-reversion bias.", "Model accuracy improves when sentiment aligns with recent price trends, suggesting sentiment interaction enhances forecasting.", "Forecast bias is most pronounced in the first 10 days of the 30-day window, indicating delayed reaction to sentiment shifts.", "True outcomes frequently dip below forecasted values after a sentiment peak, suggesting model overconfidence in upward momentum."]}
